questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Edinburgh because of the hiking opportunities, the beautiful, cozy city and the fact that everyone speaks English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! They organized meetings for Erasmus students and put you in contact with a personal student advisor.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Online meetings with student advisors.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in Pollock Halls, catered accommodation with breakfast and dinner included. Some other people lived in self-catered with shared kitchens.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Breakfast and dinner buffet in a cafeteria.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed living in catered accommodation and met a lot of my friends in the cafeteria. It was nice to see other students for breakfast and dinner.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing was way too expensive in my opinion, and it wouldn't have been sustainable for me to stay longer than one semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Uni of Edinburgh gave us all the information we needed. Most registration were online, but we had one in person registration in the welcome week.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Meeting with student advisor - Edinburgh in general seems to have a lot of support offers and staff is very kind.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get all the courses I wanted, but it worked out fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be persistent. It pays to keep sending mails/calling the student advisors since they don't really do any waiting lists, so you just have to be lucky with your timing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were interesting, possibly a bit lower academic level than in Copenhagen, but it's hard to compare because the teaching styles and exam types are different.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More class discussions - I didn't always find the discussions fruitful, but I think it was a good challenge for me to try to engage more and explore my own beliefs and opinions on the theories.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Emotion
Popular Music, Technology and Society
Social Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Popular Music, Technology and Society - definitely. Nick Prior is an amazing teacher, very kind and just brilliant and nerdy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was very expensive - but keep in mind that it includes breakfast and dinner.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many! Look at Edinburgh University Student Association instagram or website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend joining the hillwalking club and pleasance gym - they have some really nice gym classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on a day trip to the Pentlands - it's a short bus ride from Edinburgh and very pretty. 
Visit cute bookstores and coffee shops
Take a weekend trip to the highlands - Isle of Skye is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and join some societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None - people are very kind and open.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and the chill vibe of the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you bring enough money for all the fun opportunities
Bring outdoor clothes and explore the Scottish nature
Be open minded and try new things:)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The wonderful people I've met. I have had such an amazing and special time in Edinburgh. The city now holds a very special place in my heart.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I struggled with the essay deadlines - but that could have been avoided if I had prioritized my time differently throughout the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
